title: Who gave him that flower
html_source:
Bloom’s flower was in the letter he received from his romantic penpal Martha in Chapter 5.
“He tore the flower gravely from its pinhold smelt its almost no smell and placed it in his heart pocket.”

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: I think the passage running from ‘I wonder is he awake’ to ‘the sweety kind of paste’ refers to Boylan, not Bloom, Molly doesn’t know about Bloom’s flower from Martha Clifford; she is referring to Boylan’s red carnation that he picked up at the florist in episode 5 of the Wandering Rocks chapter; he wears it all afternoon and it is often referred to (e.g. by one of the barmaids in the Ormond Bar). In the Sirens chapter, Boylan orders a sloe gin and just before leaving the bar at 4pm, he ‘drankoff his tiny chalice, sucking the last fat violet syrupy drops’, suggesting to Molly a ‘sweety kind of past’.
